chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Bill Winston, the Topps drummer, now in Hawaii; Hubert Laws's band
summary: Collins recalls another Topps drummer, Bill Winston, whom he met in Honolulu a year earlier while touring with Hubert Laws, and tries to remember other band members.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: She loved her. She was a tremendous entertainer. Just a tremendous entertainer. But I had -- I don't know how I could have forgotten Albert Topps because it was a very important time in my life too. Because Albert -- they -- we had another drummer working there with us by the name of Bill Winston who was quite a musician. He played with Scoops' brother's band, Ed Carey. They had a band in Chicago. I didn't play with Ed Carey, they were a little older than I was, you know. I was a little boy, they wouldn't let

me in, you know.

But Scoops wasn't much older than I was, but he got in because it was his brother, you know. But Bill Winston is now living in Hawaii, he's in Honolulu, and he's the president -- he was the president of the union, the musician's union there now. But I don't think he is now, he's still affiliated with the union in some capacity. As a matter of fact I was over there last year with Hubert Laws. We did a couple of concerts at the University of Hawaii and I saw Bill Winston. Now, in the band was with Hubert Laws his brother Ronnie Laws, Harvey Mason, and the pianist, what's his -- you know, wrote "Roth Pensativa". He was with the High Lo's. Very fine pianist. Any way, it was a very good band. I'll think of his name in a moment. So that was about a little over a year ago. I saw Bill once in there.
So you see, Pat, I do exist.
Was Bill Winston in Albert Laws band?
No, he was -- Oh, I saw him there. No, I told you he was a drummer. Harvey Mason was the drummer with Hubert Laws. You don't know Harvey Mason.
Yes, I know, but Bill Winston. Was he in --
He was in Albert Topps' band at the last time. The last time I saw him was in Hawaii, and as I told

you, he at one time was the president of the union there. Now he is -- has some official capacity with the union. I don't know, he's not president. But I saw him about a year ago, and he was just so happy to see me. We just -- matter of fact he cried when I left, you know, he was --you know, one of those things.
Clara Fisher was the pianist. That's what I'm trying to say.
Yes. And Hubert Laws, yeah, with our group.
I meant, you weren't trying to see if you could remember anybody else and in Elbert Albert Topps' band.
No, I can't remember. I only remember Dan Grissom, Elbert Albert Topps -- well, it was a small band. My mother would play piano, and --
